claims.claim: The stated parity-explicit candidate spans a doubly-even [9,4,4] code with 16 words, active coordinate 9 and coordinate 8 fixed at zero.
claims.gap: Not a claim about the current live repository.

claims.claim: XOR updates by codewords preserve the coset x_0+C, so arbitrarily deep histories do not escape the 16-label sector.
claims.confidence: high under the stated transition law

claims.claim: Full C-valued move histories have 16^n depth-n leaves, a countable finite-prefix tree, and continuum-many infinite histories.
support: cardinality and endpoint-count arguments in note Sections 3.1-3.2
claims.confidence: high for the full branching construction
claims.gap: Restricted grammars require separate path-count analysis; finite tests are not proofs of infinity.

claims.claim: Normalized consistent conditional branch probabilities define a unique cylinder-generated infinite-path probability measure in the finite-alphabet setting.
claims.confidence: high under the stated consistency and terminal-handling assumptions
claims.gap: No claim that arbitrary quantum protocols share such a classical measure.

claims.claim: The codeword-stack extension has infinitely many configurations distinguishable by future legal pop sequences despite identical local labels.
claims.confidence: high under the proposed stack semantics
claims.gap: An added mathematical construction, not derived cosmological dynamics or a novelty claim.

claims.claim: Unit total mass at every independently normalized horizon does not guarantee compatible prefix distributions.
The specified recorded-history map is an isometry, but per-parent norm conservation alone is not general unitarity or evidence of quantum branching physics.
claims.confidence: high for the algebra; physical interpretation unverified
claims.gap: No closed-system infinite-limit model, interference experiment, or decoherence derivation was supplied.

claims.claim: A growing event graph can provide unbounded global configurations with local code closure, but event ordering, covariance and geometry need independent constraints.
claims.confidence: high for algebraic closure and acyclicity of the specified growth candidate; physical relevance unresolved
claims.gap: No event-graph simulation, continuum limit, or physical bridge derived.

claims.claim: The uniform baseline has 4n bits of history entropy but only 4 bits of endpoint entropy for n>=1.
claims.confidence: high under uniform independent codeword moves
claims.gap: Not a thermodynamic or cosmological entropy claim.

claims.claim: Uniform full-code branching counts and endpoint laws are generic to rank-4 binary additive groups rather than ASH-specific advantages.
claims.gap: Comparative geometry-sensitive, decoding-sensitive, and physical-observable experiments not run.
